def-meshfree-cell-quadrature-and-fill-ra:
## Definition

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open. Write $B(x,r)$ for the open Euclidean ball from [[def-metric-ball]] with distance induced by [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. A family of cells is **locally finite** here when every compact subset of $\Omega$ meets only finitely many cells. A bounded set is **Jordan measurable** when its Jordan inner and outer contents agree ([[def-jordan-inner-and-outer-content]]). A **cell particle rule** is a locally finite family of bounded Jordan-measurable cells $C_j\subseteq\Omega$ whose interiors are disjoint and whose union covers $\Omega$ up to their shared boundaries, together with nodes $x_j\in C_j$ and positive volumes $V_j=\int 1_{C_j}$. The cell volume integral is Riemann-defined and equals the Jordan content ([[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]]). Its fill radius is $h=\sup_j\sup_{y\in C_j}|y-x_j|$, using the Euclidean norm from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Assume finite constants $C_V,C_L>0$ satisfy $V_j\le C_Vh^d$ and the local volume bound

$$\sum_{j:C_j\cap B(x,r)\ne\varnothing}V_j\le C_L(r+h)^d$$

for every $x\in\mathbb R^d$ and $r>0$. For continuous $g:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ with compact support contained in $\Omega$ (support as in [[def-support-and-compactly-supported-riemann-integral-in-rn]]), define $Q_hg=\sum_jV_jg(x_j)$; local finiteness makes this sum finite. At kernel width $\varepsilon$, an evaluation point is **interior** when $B(x,R\varepsilon+2h)\subset\Omega$. For periodic calculations, use the periodic extensions of the field and particle rule on $\mathbb R^d$, so no kernel support is truncated.

The cell rule is integration-compatible: for every continuous $g:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ with compact support contained in $\Omega$, only finitely many cells meet $\operatorname{supp}(g)$, every cell integral appearing below is Riemann-defined, and
$$\int_\Omega g(y)\,dy=\sum_{j:C_j\cap\operatorname{supp}(g)\ne\varnothing}\int_{C_j}g(y)\,dy.$$
This finite partition identity is part of the quadrature data.
def-scaled-symmetric-compact-kernel-fami:
## Definition

Fix an integer $d\ge1$. An **admissible smoothing kernel** is a radial function $W\in C_c^2(\mathbb R^d,[0,\infty))$, supported in the closed Euclidean ball $\overline B(0,R)$ of some radius $R>0$ ([[def-metric-ball]]), with $\int_{\mathbb R^d}W(z)\,dz=1$. Here radial means $W(z)=w(|z|)$ for some function $w:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, and $C_c^2$ means twice continuously differentiable with compact support. All vector norms are the Euclidean norm from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], and $\|D^2W\|_\infty$ uses the induced operator norm. Throughout this pair, $L^\infty$ norms are suprema of Euclidean norms, and norms of multilinear derivatives are the induced operator norms. Compactly supported integrals use [[def-support-and-compactly-supported-riemann-integral-in-rn]], where $\operatorname{supp}f$ is the closure of the set on which $f$ is nonzero.

For $\varepsilon>0$ define the scaled kernel $W_\varepsilon(z)=\varepsilon^{-d}W(z/\varepsilon)$. Write $M_0=\|W\|_\infty$, $M_1=\|\nabla W\|_\infty$, $M_2=\|D^2W\|_\infty$, $m_2=\int |z|^2W(z)\,dz$, and $m_3=\int |z|^3|\nabla W(z)|\,dz$. These constants are finite because their integrands are continuous and compactly supported.

For continuous $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$, define the full-space smoother and its kernel-gradient operator by
$$S_\varepsilon f(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}f(x-z)W_\varepsilon(z)\,dz,\qquad D_\varepsilon f(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}f(y)\nabla W_\varepsilon(x-y)\,dy.$$
Both integrals exist as compactly supported Riemann integrals for each fixed $x$; the vector integral defining $D_\varepsilon f$ is taken componentwise.

This page fixes $\varepsilon$ in the finite-particle system. Limits $\varepsilon\to0$ are used only in the stated kernel-bias and joint-refinement results.
def-regularized-conservative-sph-system:
## Definition

Fix d,N≥1, positive masses m_1,…,m_N, ε>0, the kernel W_ε from [[def-scaled-symmetric-compact-kernel-family]], and a pressure map P∈C¹((0,∞)×R,R). Positions q_i and velocities v_i lie in R^d with the Euclidean inner product from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], and specific internal energies e_i lie in R. Define

$$\rho_i(q)=\sum_{j=1}^Nm_jW_\varepsilon(q_i-q_j),\qquad p_i=P(\rho_i,e_i),\qquad A_i=\frac{p_i}{\rho_i^2}.$$

The state domain is U={ (q,v,e): ρ_i(q)>0 for every i }. On U, the fixed-width semidiscrete system is

$$\dot q_i=v_i,\qquad \dot v_i=-\sum_{j=1}^Nm_j(A_i+A_j)\nabla W_\varepsilon(q_i-q_j),\qquad \dot e_i=A_i\sum_{j=1}^Nm_j(v_i-v_j)\cdot\nabla W_\varepsilon(q_i-q_j).$$

A controlled tube is a compact subset of U on which ρ_i≥ρ_*>0 for every i. The system is semidiscrete: time remains continuous while the spatial state is represented by finitely many particles. It has fixed masses and fixed ε, includes the displayed matched internal-energy equation, and contains no artificial viscosity. No continuum Euler convergence is part of this definition.
lem-cellwise-particle-quadrature-oscilla:
## Statement

Let g be compactly supported and Lipschitz with constant L_g, meaning |g(y)−g(x)|≤L_g|y−x|, and use the cells and nodes of [[def-meshfree-cell-quadrature-and-fill-radius]]. Define osc_C(g)=sup_{y,z∈C}|g(y)−g(z)| and let J_g={j:C_j∩supp(g)≠∅}. Then

$$\left|\int_\Omega g(y)dy-Q_hg\right|\le\sum_{j\in J_g}V_j\operatorname{osc}_{C_j}(g)\le 2hL_g\sum_{j\in J_g}V_j.$$
lem-symmetric-kernel-moment-cancellation:
## Statement

For the kernel W and its scaled family W_ε of [[def-scaled-symmetric-compact-kernel-family]], the first moment vanishes: ∫zW(z) dz=0 and ∫zW_ε(z) dz=0 for every ε>0.
lem-compact-kernel-derivative-moment-ide:
## Statement

For W from [[def-scaled-symmetric-compact-kernel-family]] and coordinate indices j,k,l,

$$\int \partial_kW(z)\,dz=0,\qquad \int z_j\partial_kW(z)\,dz=-\delta_{jk},\qquad \int z_jz_l\partial_kW(z)\,dz=0.$$

Also m₃=∫|z|³|∇W(z)|dz is finite.
lem-scaled-kernel-moments-and-derivative:
## Statement

For the scaled kernels of [[def-scaled-symmetric-compact-kernel-family]] and every ε>0, supp W_ε⊂\overline B(0,Rε), ∫W_ε=1, ∫zW_ε(z)dz=0, and ∫|z|²W_ε(z)dz=ε²m₂. Pointwise, ∇W_ε(z)=ε^(−d−1)∇W(z/ε) and D²W_ε(z)=ε^(−d−2)D²W(z/ε); consequently their sup norms equal ε^(−d−1)M₁ and ε^(−d−2)M₂.
lem-sph-pair-forces-antisymmetric-and-ce:
## Statement

For the system in [[def-regularized-conservative-sph-system]], set g_ij=∇W_ε(q_i−q_j) and define the force contribution F_ij=−m_im_j(A_i+A_j)g_ij. Radial evenness gives g_ji=−g_ij and g_ii=0, so for i≠j, F_ji=−F_ij; also F_ij is parallel to q_i−q_j (the zero vector is allowed).
thm-second-order-meshfree-convolution-bi:
## Statement

Let f∈C²(R^d) have bounded Hessian and define S_εf(x)=∫f(x−z)W_ε(z)dz. Then for every ε>0 and x∈R^d,

$$|S_\varepsilon f(x)-f(x)|\le \frac{m_2}{2}\varepsilon^2\|D^2f\|_\infty.$$
lem-regularized-sph-vector-field-lipschi:
## Statement

Let K be a compact convex subset of the positive-density domain of [[def-regularized-conservative-sph-system]]. Use ||z||#=max_i{|q_i|,|v_i|,|e_i|}, M=Σ_im_i, V=sup_{z∈K}max_i|v_i|, K₁=||∇W_ε||∞, K₂=||D²W_ε||∞, and a(ρ,e)=P(ρ,e)/ρ². Define A₀=max_{z∈K,,i}|a(ρ_i(q),e_i)|, A_ρ=max_{z∈K,,i}|∂_ρa(ρ_i(q),e_i)|, A_e=max_{z∈K,,i}|∂_ea(ρ_i(q),e_i)|, and A₁=2MK₁A_ρ+A_e. These maxima are finite by compactness, positivity of the densities, and continuity. Then the full state vector field F is Lipschitz on K with constant

$$L=\max\{1,\ M(2K_1A_1+4A_0K_2),\ 2MVA_1K_1+2MA_0K_1+4MA_0VK_2\}.$$
prop-sph-conserves-linear-and-angular-mo:
## Statement

Every C¹ solution of [[def-regularized-conservative-sph-system]] conserves total linear momentum P=Σ_im_iv_i and the antisymmetric angular-momentum tensor J=Σ_im_i(q_i⊗v_i−v_i⊗q_i), where (a⊗b)_kl=a_kb_l.
prop-sph-matched-internal-energy-conserv:
## Statement

Every C¹ solution of [[def-regularized-conservative-sph-system]] conserves H=Σ_im_i(|v_i|²/2+e_i). The identity uses exactly the displayed matched internal-energy equation.
thm-first-derivative-meshfree-convolutio:
## Statement

Let f∈C³(R^d) have bounded third derivative and define D_εf(x)=∫f(y)∇W_ε(x−y)dy. Then for every ε>0 and x∈R^d,

$$|D_\varepsilon f(x)-\nabla f(x)|\le \frac{m_3}{6}\varepsilon^2\|D^3f\|_\infty,$$

where ||D³f||∞ is the supremum of the operator norm of the trilinear derivative.
thm-meshfree-particle-kernel-quadrature-:
## Statement

Assume the cell rule of [[def-meshfree-cell-quadrature-and-fill-radius]], h≤ε≤1, x is interior, and f∈C¹(R^d) is bounded with bounded first derivative. Define

$$Q^0_{\varepsilon,h}f(x)=\sum_jV_jf(x_j)W_\varepsilon(x-x_j),\qquad Q^1_{\varepsilon,h}f(x)=\sum_jV_jf(x_j)\nabla W_\varepsilon(x-x_j).$$

Let S_εf(x)=∫f(y)W_ε(x−y)dy and D_εf(x)=∫f(y)∇W_ε(x−y)dy. There is C=C(d,R,C_L,W), independent of ε,h,x, such that

$$|Q^0_{\varepsilon,h}f(x)-S_\varepsilon f(x)|\le Ch\bigl(\|\nabla f\|_\infty+\varepsilon^{-1}\|f\|_\infty\bigr),$$

$$|Q^1_{\varepsilon,h}f(x)-D_\varepsilon f(x)|\le Ch\bigl(\varepsilon^{-1}\|\nabla f\|_\infty+\varepsilon^{-2}\|f\|_\infty\bigr).$$
cor-meshfree-joint-refinement-consistenc:
## Statement

Assume the hypotheses of [[thm-meshfree-particle-kernel-quadrature-error]] and let f∈C³(R^d) have bounded derivatives. There are constants C₀,C₁, independent of ε,h and the interior point x, such that

$$|Q^0_{\varepsilon,h}f(x)-f(x)|\le C_0\varepsilon^2\|D^2f\|_\infty+C_1h\bigl(\|\nabla f\|_\infty+\varepsilon^{-1}\|f\|_\infty\bigr),$$

$$|Q^1_{\varepsilon,h}f(x)-\nabla f(x)|\le C_0\varepsilon^2\|D^3f\|_\infty+C_1h\bigl(\varepsilon^{-1}\|\nabla f\|_\infty+\varepsilon^{-2}\|f\|_\infty\bigr).$$

Thus ε→0 and h/ε²→0 suffice for both value and derivative errors to vanish uniformly at interior points. Constants depend only on the fixed kernel, dimension, and cell regularity.
thm-regularized-sph-local-wellposedness:
## Statement

For the system of [[def-regularized-conservative-sph-system]], U={z:ρ_i(q)>0 for every i} is open and its finite-dimensional vector field F is continuous and locally Lipschitz on U. From each initial state z₀∈U there is a unique local C¹ solution.
thm-forward-euler-global-error-on-contro:
## Statement

Use the state norm ||z||#=max_i{|q_i|,|v_i|,|e_i|} on the finite-dimensional state space, and dist#(z,Kᶜ)=inf_{y∉K}||z−y||#. Let z(t), 0≤t≤T, be the unique solution from [[thm-regularized-sph-local-wellposedness]] and let K⊂U be compact and convex, with dist#(z(t),Kᶜ)≥δ>0 for every t. Assume B,L≥0, ||F(z)||#≤B and Lip#(F|K)≤L. For h=T/n set Z₀=z(0) and Z_{k+1}=Z_k+hF(Z_k). Put E_h=(Bh/2)(exp(LT)−1), which is zero when L=0. If E_h<δ, then every Euler state Z_k lies in K and

$$\max_{0\le k\le n}\|Z_k-z(kh)\|_\#\le E_h.$$

The tube margin and exact-path hypothesis are explicit. This result makes no energy- or momentum-conservation claim for the Euler time discretization.
